title: [VIC] Sigenergy 27kWh Battery + 10kW Inverter from $9000, Full Home Backup from $9,900 (after Rebate, $1,000 Deposit) @ PA Power
body:
Deal: [VIC] Sigenergy 27kWh Battery + 10kW Inverter from $9000, Full Home Backup from $9,900 (after Rebate, $1,000 Deposit) @ PA Power

[Avi0001] I am getting this week - Fox ESS latest 28kw battery latest version and Fox 10kw hybrid invertor in $6200 after rebate in Victoria.
Note - Panels are not included.
[tritorius] Who is that through? I've been looking for the same deal since missing out on the May cutoff.
[Avi0001] Green savings told me just now $5800.
Battery - EQ4800. Battery and Q7 new technology
And Fox 10kw hybrid inverter.
[samehada] EQ4800 is the old model with current limiting issue at low temperature. CQ7 is the newer model.
[Avi0001] @samehada: Sorry I wrote mistakenly its Q7 with 4x in.
[samehada] @Avi0001: You wrote Battery - EQ4800.
There is no Q7 model with FoxESS, only CQ7 which is the new one.
[Avi0001] @samehada: He just told me over the phone because I told them to reduce the price and give me some better deal. So I beleive its CQ7.
[Avi0001] @samehada: I have just got the contract with updated models so you can check the screenshot.
https://files.ozbargain.com.au/upload/478432/130210/screensh…
[MilkteaS] Hi For Fox ESS Battery in Victoria, we are happy to beat price :)
[cornflakes] Are there options for backup with the Fox like we have with the Sigenergy gateway?
E: nevermind, just read the comments below.
[blaast] What fully off-grid systems do you have?
[Yamahar6] Im getting same plus 6.6kwh panels Jinko for $7k.
[Tejas57] ive got a sigenergy system. my advise - spring for the gateway. our power went out about 3 weeks ago for 3 hours and we didn't even know until the nbn went down too
[MilkteaS] Higly recommended. That why we put further discount for gateway package.
[soupratt] Any good gateway or full home backup for the FoxESS CQ7/10kw inverter you guys installed for me ? I didn't do it at the time as it would have delayed installation but I hear Fox is coming out/or has come out with their own gateway ?
As a side note, these guys installed my system and everything went very smoothly. Very happy with the CQ7.
[MilkteaS] Not yet in Australia. It is released in UK for months
[soupratt] @MilkteaS: Worth waiting for rather than doing selective circuit backup ?
[MilkteaS] @soupratt: I'll say box which provide full home backup is the best option, however either Fox ESS AU and us have no idea when it could pass AU standard.
[soupratt] @MilkteaS: No rush. Please keep us posted re the Foxess Gateway
[MilkteaS] Our solar teams in QLD and WA are working on industry project at the moment, that's why I only post Vic at the moment. :)
[ToastySteve] Don't mean to hijack, but any battery deals coming to QLD?
I'm keen as mustard.
[MilkteaS] Our solar teams in QLD and WA are working on industry project at the moment, that's why I only post Vic at the moment.
[MilkteaS] For smaller system, yes.
Large system used to be only size aviliable on market. Following the rebate drop after 28kW, Smaller system would getting more popular.
[podilamaya] @MilkteaS
Do you install Victron inverters for Grid-tie system ?
[skysky] I literally just got a 32kwh Sigenergy system installed 2 weeks ago. And this package looks like it uses the newer BAT10 batteries. Why so cheap?
Can you quote on adding a second stack or batteries? Or the price of an additional module?
Also, what would the cost be if I wanted to upgrade existing grid connection to support minimum of 80A or 20kw import from grid?
[MilkteaS] The newer battery is BAT10, which is 9kW each. I dont think it can form a 32kWh system?
Yes we can. However the rebate only applied to first system, and at this stage only one battery sysytem could exist in one property.
Upgrading existing grid connection to support minimum of 80A or 20kw import from grid highly depends on your energy distributor. Use https://www.energy.vic.gov.au/households/find-your-energy-di… to contact them directly.
[skysky] No I have the older BAT8. I'm saying what you are offering is the newer version.
My distributor is United Energy. Apart from the distributor, I don't believe my current wiring is sufficient. 16mm cross sections
[whitelie] The 9kwh modules are cheaper than the 8's now.
Should have been able to get 36kwh for the same price
[travisty18] I wish we could get deals like this in QLD!
[unco] If going for the full home backup with gateway, do you remove the existing inverter and it get DC-coupled to existing panels?
Will the battery be able to be charged from solar during a blackout?
Very keen on a deal like this.
[MilkteaS] Both dc and ac coupling can be installed with gateway.
For ac coupling gateway, the battery is not able to be charged from solar during a blackout.
For dc, yes. However it could be much more expensive.
[unco] Do you have a rough indication on cost for DC coupling? And how much is the travel fee?
Also just a side note the prices in the google form with gateway don’t match the prices stated in this deal.
[87percent] Can you quote for solar upgrade, with inverter/battery install?
[MilkteaS] Generally speaking it takes $40/Panel of removal, and 600$ for removing old solar string inverter.
We can quote more detailed one for sure.
[effraye] How much for 8.45kw worth of anko panels?
[ChaseTheSun] Do you also do the Sig DC charger, 12.5KW ? how much extra is it?
[MilkteaS] We only provide Sigen EV DC Charging Module 25 kW at this stage.
[pooks] how much for Sigenergy 18kWh Battery Package: SigenStor EC 10.0 single phase + 2 x SigenStor BAT10 battery modules+Full house Backup Gateway, postcode 3044
[saliya] NSW too? This looks like a fair deal to me, I'm looking to add a second stack as well as add a battery for my mother
[Tazzaaa] Sounds like a great deal. I got a few quotes here in SA and they are all hovering around the 17-18.5k mark. 24kwh battery, 10kw of solar with a 10kw inverter.
am i getting ripped off or are there major price differences between states?
[jackwilk] Yup same here. 6.6kw solar with 16kwh battery is 13k, then bigger 10kw solar with 24kwh battery 18k. LONGI / GOODWE system.
[poiterbad] Yeah, we need some of these good deals in SA
[downhillmtbr] Currently have a 16kwh system in vic, with 13kw of solar.
Any reason to add an additional battery? Seems to be pretty well sized to fit our generation and consumption (considering how little sunlight we get in winter). But feel like I'm missing something with everyone installing 48kwh systems.
Is there just a short term arbitrate to re-sell energy back to the grid in summer etc? or import overnight and export later in the day or something?
[chrismheath] Once you've used the rebate there's probably no point adding more battery modules. I have a 40kwh (5 x 8bat) unit with 14.7kwp of solar, got it when the rebate went up to 50kwh. Also with a provider that does 3 hour free window, also has reasonable rates selling back between 6 to 9.
The larger batteries are useful to me since: high usage household, have EVs (can take some from the battery, put into the EV and fill it up with solar/3 hour window during the day) and ability to sell back when we're not using it all up. If some people have more unstable connections a bigger battery may mean a better chance of getting through if their power goes out for long periods of time.
No chance I'd increase/upgrade storage without the rebate though, easily a financial loss.
[effraye] EV is the point increasing the battery makes sense
[downhillmtbr] even if one has a cheap i.e 8c overnight rate?
[chrismheath] @downhillmtbr: For my use case I drive probably around 100kwh worth a week, so thats either $8/week or $0/week if I can basically move energy around (battery to car) a bit a day.
At the point I got my modules, they were $2k per 8kwh battery (which is ridiculously cheap, still don't know how they did it) post rebate. From a pure maths perspective, $8/week * 50 = $400 (lets say couple weeks of not driving total), 5 years breakeven excluding whatever money I would've made from it being in the offset.
I was also not convinced at the time that the 8c/kwh (or the 3 free hour) would stay around at their rate, but so far have been proven wrong about one of them.
[downhillmtbr] Thanks for the reply.
This battery was purchased pre-rebate if that changes anything :)
[chrismheath] Not 100% sure if you can claim more battery bits if you had one before, and then you'd have to check if whatever you've got is compatible.
Really then boils down to usage and future usage. I think this game of being able to arbitrage electricity won't be around that much longer as larger wholesale battery systems come online, so then just comes down to if using the extra power would mean less costs over time.
Our usage was lowish before we got our system installed (excluding the EV, had it for a few months before the system) but ballooned once the wifey had free power for aircons in the house. On a colder day (Melbourne) we're probably using 40-60kwh, plus whatever for the car.
[dufflover] Got a 15kwh battery here, unfortunately before the whole battery rebate policy was announced and all that, and the recent weather of late has left it high and dry. So many days of bad weather the battery hasn't hit 100% for a few weeks.
We don't have the free energy window plans because when we did the maths so they only worked out better with a big 40k type battery, big enough to charge and export like with Globird. That said the math also clearly says given what we have and spent, we could import the shortage in battery capacity for yonks and still have paid less than getting a larger subsided battery now.
But yes a part of my head won't let go of the jealousy of not having a massive battery like people have been able to get.
[meeeeeeee] Hi,
Already have a 7kwh battery on one of three phases, installed pre rebates
CT clamp is only on the one phase, other two not backed up or or monitored at all
Would you be willing to leave this in place and add the new Ac coupled system?
almost everyone else I have spoken to will only install on the condition the old battery is removed
[oztite] Hi, if I don't have a solar system, can I still get a battery to charge it during off-peak period (e.g. those cheap overnight EV charging plans) and use the stored electricity during more expensive peak period?
[effraye] Good call once the solar saver thing starts in vic in October
[Franc-T] WTF travel fee for greater melbourne.
Good luck with that, im out.
[effraye] Diesel utes/vans to carry these heavy af batteries
[Franc-T] Wherever they go they have to carry batteries. I dont understand your point.
[AU1] We have a 6.6 / 5kwh Fronius Primo solar setup, can this be a simple add on?
[OZBsince2018] Pretty expensive.
I recently paid $5,800 for 26KW GoodWe battery plus 10KW 3 phase inverter in Sydney, including installation.
[nicolascage] During my research I found prices for solar battery were more in vic than other states
[OZBsince2018] But definitely not 50% more than NSW prices. Plus GoodWe is a better brand and name in Australia
[merriweather] That sounds like a good deal, who did you get that through?
[OZBsince2018] Not only that, I got $1,000 VPP rebate for joining the VPP program via Origin and their partner, plus $200 credit from Origin. So net it only cost me $4,600.
Will share the details here later.
[eggboi] Battery seems less and less worth it - providers jacking up daily supply charges, more people on batteries mean less expensive spikes overnight. break-even assumes KWH pricing won't drop, and the battery will last 10+ years and not drop much capacity. Here in Qld anyway. Maybe in SA there's a better economic situation for batteries.
[effraye] QLD prob gets more sun than we do in VIC this time of year and as a result the battery is a no brainer for us, we pay 88c daily supply charge and offpeak rate is 15.5c/kw/hr, i charge to 75% and then hope to fill the rest of a 32kw battery on 3-9kw of sun during our wet and gloomy melb winter.. works a treat to avoid peak 3-9pm at 27c/kw/hr and charge the car overnight after ~50km on the road every day.
[smurfy] You bring this deal to QLD, i will get 2 x 27kw batteries. At the moment i havent seen a deal worth taking.
[k336] "6.6 kW Solar PV System (17 × Jinko Solar 475W Panels) $4,000 installed (Solar Vic $1,400 rebate might applied,after rebate $2,600)"
17x 475 = 8075W
Can you clarify this price is for 6.6kW or 8kW?
[paulrozza] We have a single phase Solaredge 10KWh Inverter with 2 x Solaredge DC coupled 9KWh batteries with whole home backup and around 18.5KWh of panels on the roof. Is it possible to AC couple the Sigenstor to increase storage capacity and control via the Solaredge inverter?
[GOB] I have 16kwh on the roof and a Sig inverter in Brisbane. Keen for a battery.
[Meulsie] Do you also do changeover from gas hot water to electric? Roughly how much is that?
[Tommohalby] They are not on Solar Quotes (or I couldn't find them). I normally use that as a baseline. Any reason not on there or a reason not to worry. What do people think?
[Tanvry] wow, under 10k for a 27kwh battery and 10kw inverter?
[mrhugo] I don't understand why clauses like the the 30-Day claim window exist. So if I go on holidays for 2 months, and don't check the app, I abandoned the right to make a warranty claim, wtf?
https://www.sigenergy.com/en/pdfView/sigenergy-data-warranty…
page 3/6 : Please make the claim within 30 days from the failure date, otherwise SIGENERGY will treat it
as you have abandoned the right to make a warranty claim.
Edit page 5 has the usual Important Note:Australian Consumer Law clause so if the unit stops working, it is legally classified as a major failure. So I guess you could fight it, but still why bother with the clause on 3/6, maybe they are hoping some customers don't exercise their rights.
[ordinarygreenbottle] Looks like a very competitive offer.
I'm in Melbourne with annual usage of around 6-7,000 kWh.
A few questions:
Is the advertised package genuinely the system you'd recommend for a household like mine, or would you often suggest a smaller battery after reviewing the customer's usage?
Roughly how many Sigenergy systems has PA Power installed to date?
What workmanship warranty do you provide on your installations?
For a typical single-storey Melbourne home, what are the most common additional costs beyond the advertised price?
Thanks
[downhillmtbr] How much would it be for just the batteries with an existing SigEnergy inverter / stack?
Thanks
[rzy6cn] Sigenergy C/P Ratio is relatively low before 1st May but now the price become much more competitive.
